title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Air Detector Alarm or Air Cannot Be Cleared From the Fluid Path
description: Troubleshoot visible air, loose connections, depleted fluid sources, disposable positioning, and priming problems before suspecting an air-detection system failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Stop Unreliable Delivery
steps.instructions: Do not continue rapid infusion when the device reports air or when visible air remains in the patient fluid path. Transfer therapy to another verified method as clinically appropriate before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The patient is protected from an unreliable or air-containing infusion pathway.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Alarm Condition
steps.instructions: Record the exact displayed alarm or message and determine whether: Air is visibly present The alarm occurs during priming The alarm occurs during active flow The alarm repeats with an apparently air-free set Do not dismiss repeated air alarms without verification. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as true visible air, incomplete priming, or possible false detection.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Fluid Source
steps.instructions: Verify that the source container contains sufficient fluid and that its outlet remains immersed or otherwise positioned to prevent air entry. Check for an emptied bag, loose spike, loose connector, or source change that may have introduced air. Expected outcome: A continuous fluid supply is available without an obvious route for air entry.

steps.title: 4. Inspect All External Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the disposable pathway from the fluid source through the reservoir and toward the patient-line connection. Look for: Loose connections Partially seated fittings Cracked components Improperly closed ports Disconnected tubing Visible air accumulation Expected outcome: All external connections are secure and no obvious source of air ingress remains.

steps.title: 5. Check Disposable Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify that the disposable is loaded correctly and that tubing passing through air-detection areas is fully seated, straight, and free of twists, folds, contamination, or deformation. Do not place foreign material between tubing and accessible detection surfaces. Expected outcome: Tubing is correctly positioned at all accessible detection points.

steps.title: 6. Reprime the Disposable Path
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from patient use, perform the normal accessible priming process using an appropriate test fluid. Observe whether visible air moves out of the disposable pathway and whether fluid completely occupies the intended path. Expected outcome: Visible air clears and the air alarm resets. If the alarm does not return during functional testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Replace a Suspect Disposable
steps.instructions: If air repeatedly collects despite secure connections and an adequate fluid source, replace the disposable with a known-good compatible set. Inspect the removed set for leakage, loose bonding, distorted tubing, or other visible defects. Expected outcome: A known-good disposable primes without persistent air accumulation or false alarms.

steps.title: 8. Compare Alarm Behavior With a Controlled Bench Setup
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate nonpatient test setup, operate the device with a known-good disposable and controlled fluid source. Observe whether an air alarm occurs when the visible fluid path is completely primed. Expected outcome: No air alarm occurs with a correctly primed known-good setup. If normal operation is restored, the external disposable or setup was the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that: The fluid path remains visibly free of air The alarm does not recur unexpectedly Fluid delivery remains stable Audible and visual alarm indications remain functional Do not return the device to service if air detection is intermittent or unreliable. Expected outcome: The RI-2 operates normally with a fully primed path and stable alarm behavior.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Repeated False Air Detection
steps.instructions: If the device repeatedly reports air with a correctly installed, visibly air-free known-good disposable, remove it from service. Do not bypass, obstruct, disable, or alter the air-detection system. Expected outcome: A potentially unreliable air-detection system is prevented from returning to clinical use until evaluated.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported repeated air detector alarms during setup of the RI-2.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose external disposable connection allowing air to enter the fluid path.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was corrected, the disposable was reprimed, and the unit operated without recurring air alarms during functional testing.

helpfulDetails: Whether alarm occurred during prime or flow

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Battery Will Not Charge or Transport Operation Fails
description: Troubleshoot AC supply, power connections, charging indications, battery state, transport setup, and runtime problems before suspecting an internal charging-system failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing Battery Operation
steps.instructions: Do not perform transport or battery troubleshooting while the patient depends on an RI-2 with uncertain runtime. Use stable AC power or another verified device as appropriate before removing external power. Expected outcome: Patient therapy is protected from unexpected power loss.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Battery Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem is: Battery does not appear to charge Battery runtime is unexpectedly short Unit shuts down when AC is disconnected Transport operation cannot be started Battery indication is inconsistent The device was recently stored or left disconnected Record any exact display indications. Expected outcome: The battery complaint is clearly defined and reproducible.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is connected to a known-good appropriate outlet. If permitted by facility practice, verify the outlet with another suitable device or electrical tester. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is available to the RI-2.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Power Cord and Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the external power cord, plug, strain relief, and device-side connection for: Cuts Fraying Bent components Loose connection Heat damage Contamination Remove damaged power components from service. Expected outcome: The AC connection is secure and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Verify Charging Indication
steps.instructions: Connect the device to AC power and observe the available battery or charging indication. Do not assume that an illuminated display confirms the battery is charging. Expected outcome: The device recognizes AC power and shows an appropriate charging state.

steps.title: 6. Allow Appropriate Charging Opportunity
steps.instructions: If the battery may be depleted from storage or transport use, allow it to charge in accordance with approved manufacturer guidance before evaluating runtime. Do not invent a charging duration or expected runtime. Expected outcome: The battery receives an appropriate charge before further testing.

steps.title: 7. Test Transition From AC to Battery
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use and configured for bench testing, observe its behavior when external AC power is removed. Verify that the device remains powered and indicates battery operation appropriately. Expected outcome: The RI-2 transitions to battery operation without an unexpected shutdown.

steps.title: 8. Evaluate Battery Runtime
steps.instructions: Using approved testing practices, evaluate whether battery operation is consistent enough for intended transport use. If the unit immediately shuts down or runtime is clearly inadequate compared with applicable service criteria, do not return it for transport use. Expected outcome: Battery performance meets applicable return-to-service requirements.

steps.title: 9. Inspect for Environmental or Storage Factors
steps.instructions: Check whether the unit has been exposed to: Extended storage without charging Excessive heat or cold Fluid contamination Physical impact Damaged external connections Document relevant conditions without assuming they are the cause. Expected outcome: External conditions affecting battery performance are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Charging or Runtime Failure
steps.instructions: If AC power is verified and the unit still will not charge, transition to battery, or provide acceptable runtime, remove it from service for qualified battery and charging-system evaluation. Expected outcome: The RI-2 is not returned for transport use with unreliable backup power.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the RI-2 shut down when disconnected from AC power for transport.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering confirmed that AC power was normal but the battery could not sustain device operation.
CCR.Resolution: The unit was removed from service and sent for qualified battery-system evaluation and required return-to-service testing.

helpfulDetails: Whether unit operates normally on AC

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Delivered Fluid Temperature Too Low or Heater Not Available
description: Troubleshoot heater availability, disposable setup, fluid flow, temperature sensing conditions, power, and environmental factors before suspecting an internal heating failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Appropriate Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not rely on the RI-2 for warmed rapid infusion if delivered fluid temperature appears unreliable or the heating function is unavailable. Move therapy to a verified alternative when warming is clinically required. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on an unverified warming function.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Heating is unavailable from startup Fluid warms but remains lower than expected The problem appears only at certain flow conditions A temperature-related message is displayed The complaint was based on device indication or independent observation Record the exact displayed condition. Expected outcome: The heating complaint is clearly defined before components are replaced or adjusted.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Basic Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit is connected to an appropriate power source when heater operation is expected. Inspect the power cord and connection for damage or looseness and verify normal device startup. Expected outcome: The device has stable power and no unrelated power fault is preventing heater availability.

steps.title: 4. Verify Disposable and Heat-Exchange Path Setup
steps.instructions: Inspect the disposable for correct loading through all accessible warming and fluid-routing areas. Look for: Improper seating Twisted tubing Incomplete contact with external loading surfaces Visible disposable deformation Incorrect disposable type Expected outcome: The compatible disposable is loaded correctly through the external warming pathway.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Adequate Priming
steps.instructions: Verify that the disposable fluid pathway is fully primed and that fluid, rather than trapped air, occupies the intended heat-exchange pathway. Expected outcome: The disposable is fully primed without visible air that could affect heat transfer or sensor readings.

steps.title: 6. Check Fluid Source and Flow Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that the source fluid is available and flowing normally. Note whether the complaint occurs only during unusual operating conditions, but do not invent performance limits or temperatures not specified by approved documentation. Expected outcome: Heating performance is evaluated under a stable, representative test condition.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Temperature-Sensing and Loading Areas
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible surfaces associated with disposable positioning for contamination, residue, moisture, or physical obstruction. Do not reposition internal sensors or open the heater assembly. Expected outcome: No external contamination or loading problem interferes with sensing or heat transfer.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Disposable
steps.instructions: Install a new known-good compatible disposable and use an appropriate test fluid during bench evaluation. Compare heater availability and indicated temperature behavior with the original setup. Expected outcome: Normal heating returns with the known-good disposable, identifying the original disposable or setup as the likely cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Temperature and Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using appropriate approved test equipment, verify that the unit warms fluid consistently and that displayed or measured behavior is reasonable according to applicable manufacturer criteria. Do not return the device to service based solely on the heater indicator appearing active. Expected outcome: Heating performance and temperature-related indications pass the required functional check.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Heating Failure
steps.instructions: If heating remains unavailable or temperature performance remains abnormal with stable AC power, correct setup, and a known-good disposable, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: The device is referred for service rather than used with an unreliable warming function.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the RI-2 was delivering fluid but the warming function did not appear available.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable incorrectly seated in the external heat-exchange loading path.
CCR.Resolution: The disposable was correctly reloaded, the unit resumed normal heating operation, and temperature-related functional verification passed.

helpfulDetails: Whether heater became available with known-good disposable

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Display, Control Panel, Startup, or Self-Test Failure
description: Troubleshoot power, external connections, control-panel condition, contamination, startup interruptions, and reproducible self-test failures before internal service evaluation.

steps.title: 1. Remove the Device From Patient Dependence
steps.instructions: Do not use an RI-2 with an unreadable display, unresponsive controls, incomplete startup, or failed self-test for active patient therapy. Provide a verified alternate rapid-infusion method as clinically appropriate. Expected outcome: Patient care is separated from the unreliable device.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem is: Blank display Frozen or abnormal display Unresponsive control Intermittent control response Startup that does not complete Repeated self-test failure Unexpected restart or shutdown Record exact messages and visible indications. Expected outcome: The reported electronic or startup condition is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Connect the RI-2 to a known-good appropriate AC outlet. Inspect the power connection and verify that the outlet is functioning. Expected outcome: A reliable external power source is confirmed.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Power Cord and Device
steps.instructions: Check for: Damaged cord or plug Loose connection Fluid contamination Impact damage Burn marks Unusual odor Excessive heat If smoke, heat damage, fluid intrusion, or electrical damage is evident, disconnect the unit and stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: No obvious external electrical hazard is present.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Normal Power Restart
steps.instructions: With the device removed from clinical use, shut it down and restart it using normal operator-accessible controls. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a device showing signs of internal electrical failure. Expected outcome: Startup completes normally and the display and controls become responsive. If normal operation remains stable through functional verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Control Panel
steps.instructions: Check the display and external controls for: Cracks Delamination Contamination Dried fluid Stuck controls Physical damage Objects pressing against controls Clean only using approved methods. Expected outcome: Controls are unobstructed and physically intact.

steps.title: 7. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: If external accessories or connections are present, disconnect nonessential items where appropriate and retest startup. Do not remove required safety components or enter restricted service modes. Expected outcome: The startup problem is either isolated to an external accessory or remains present with the basic device configuration.

steps.title: 8. Observe Startup and Self-Test Behavior
steps.instructions: Perform a controlled restart and document: Where startup stops Whether the same message repeats Whether alarms sound Whether controls respond Whether the display remains stable Do not invent or interpret undocumented error codes. Expected outcome: Startup either completes consistently or the failure is reproducible for service evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Full Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If startup succeeds, verify: Display readability Control-panel response Audible alarm function Disposable loading Priming Fluid delivery Temperature-related operation as appropriate Stable operation without spontaneous restart Expected outcome: The RI-2 passes complete applicable functional verification before return to service.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Electronic or Self-Test Failure
steps.instructions: Remove the device from service if the display, controls, startup sequence, or self-test remains unreliable. Do not open electronic assemblies, replace circuit boards, alter firmware, or enter unauthorized service menus as part of external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The device is held for qualified service-level evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the RI-2 powered on but the control panel was unresponsive during startup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried fluid contamination around the external control-panel surface.
CCR.Resolution: The exterior was cleaned using an approved method, controls responded normally, and the unit completed startup and functional verification successfully.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of contamination or fluid intrusion

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Disposable Set Will Not Load, Prime, or Be Recognized
description: Troubleshoot disposable installation, priming, recognition, seating, connection, and visible disposable defects before suspecting an internal loading or sensing problem.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the Rapid Infuser RI-2 while a patient depends on unreliable rapid infusion. Transfer fluid or blood-product delivery to another verified device or approved alternate method as clinically appropriate. If the disposable cannot be loaded, primed, or recognized reliably, remove the affected unit from active clinical use until evaluated. Expected outcome: Patient therapy is maintained independently of the device being troubleshot.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the disposable: Will not physically load Loads but will not remain seated Cannot complete priming Is not recognized after installation Was previously operating before the problem appeared Inspect the display for the exact message or indication without assuming an internal failure. Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced or clearly defined. If the device operates normally and the reported condition cannot be reproduced after verification, continue through final functional testing before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify Basic Device Condition and Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the unit powers normally and completes its accessible startup sequence without unrelated faults. Inspect the exterior for impact damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, or obvious mechanical damage around the disposable-loading area. Expected outcome: The unit powers normally and the loading area is externally intact. If startup fails independently of the disposable, stop and evaluate the device under the appropriate startup-failure process.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Disposable Set
steps.instructions: Remove the disposable and inspect it for: Incorrect type or incompatible disposable Torn, crushed, kinked, or deformed tubing Damaged connectors Contamination Distorted disposable components Packaging damage Improperly positioned tubing or chambers Use only an appropriate disposable intended for the RI-2. Expected outcome: The disposable is correct, undamaged, and suitable for installation. Replace a visibly defective disposable before proceeding.

steps.title: 5. Reload the Disposable Carefully
steps.instructions: With the device removed from patient use, reinstall the disposable according to its intended external routing and seating points. Verify that tubing is not trapped, crossed, twisted, stretched, or pinched and that all accessible disposable components sit fully in their intended locations. Do not force the disposable into place. Expected outcome: The disposable seats without excessive force and all accessible loading points close normally. If proper reseating corrects the issue, complete priming and functional verification; if successful, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Doors, Latches, and Accessible Loading Surfaces
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible doors, latches, guides, and seating surfaces for: Debris Dried fluid Obstruction Visible damage Components that do not close completely Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer-compatible practices. Expected outcome: The loading mechanism closes freely and completely with no visible obstruction.

steps.title: 7. Attempt Priming With a Known-Good Disposable
steps.instructions: If the initial disposable remains suspect, install a new known-good compatible disposable and use an appropriate test fluid source during bench evaluation. Observe whether the system recognizes the disposable and progresses through normal priming. Expected outcome: The known-good disposable loads, is recognized, and primes normally. If so, the original disposable was the likely cause and troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Inspect External Fluid Connections and Source Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the source container, reservoir connections, tubing connections, and clamps are arranged correctly and are not preventing filling or priming. Look for closed clamps, collapsed tubing, empty source containers, or loose connections that could interrupt the prime sequence. Expected outcome: Fluid can move freely through the externally accessible disposable pathway without an obvious restriction.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate test setup and approved fluid, verify that the RI-2: Accepts the disposable Completes priming Operates without repeated recognition or loading faults Maintains a stable external fluid path Produces expected audible and visual indications during normal operation Do not return the device to service based solely on successful loading. Expected outcome: The complete disposable-loading and priming process operates normally. If all checks pass, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Loading or Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good disposables cannot be loaded, recognized, or primed after all external causes are eliminated, stop troubleshooting. Do not bypass interlocks, alter unauthorized configuration, or disassemble internal loading or sensing mechanisms. Expected outcome: The device is removed from service for qualified evaluation rather than repeatedly tested in clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the RI-2 disposable would not complete loading or priming.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable tubing incorrectly seated in the external loading path.
CCR.Resolution: The disposable was correctly reinstalled, priming completed normally, and the unit passed functional verification before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether recognition failed before or during priming

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Door, Valve, or Roller Pump Will Not Operate
description: Troubleshoot external obstruction, disposable misloading, mechanical interference, control conditions, and visible damage affecting doors, valves, or roller-pump operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Unit From Active Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a stalled door, valve, or pumping mechanism while the patient depends on the RI-2. Move therapy to another verified device or method. Expected outcome: Patient support continues independently of the malfunctioning unit.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Function Is Not Operating
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: A door that will not open or close A latch that will not engage An accessible valve mechanism that does not actuate A roller pump that does not move during normal operation Intermittent mechanical operation Record any displayed message or abnormal sound. Expected outcome: The affected mechanical function is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for External Obstruction
steps.instructions: With the unit safely inactive, inspect accessible mechanical areas for: Misrouted tubing Disposable material caught in a door Debris Dried fluid Foreign objects Damaged disposable components Do not use excessive force. Expected outcome: No external obstruction prevents normal movement.

steps.title: 4. Remove and Inspect the Disposable
steps.instructions: Remove the disposable and determine whether the door or accessible mechanism moves normally without it where appropriate. Inspect the disposable for deformation or incorrect loading that may physically interfere with the mechanism. Expected outcome: A disposable-related obstruction is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Install a Known-Good Disposable
steps.instructions: Load a new compatible disposable correctly and verify that doors and accessible loading mechanisms close without resistance. Expected outcome: Normal mechanical operation returns with the known-good disposable. If so, continue through final verification and stop when all tests pass.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Exterior Mechanical Components
steps.instructions: Check doors, hinges, latches, guides, and accessible moving surfaces for: Cracks Bending Loose components Misalignment Evidence of impact Excessive contamination Do not disassemble mechanical assemblies. Expected outcome: Exterior components are intact and move normally.

steps.title: 7. Verify Normal Control State
steps.instructions: Confirm the device is in a normal operating state and is not being prevented from operating by another active alarm, incomplete disposable setup, open door, or startup condition. Do not enter restricted service menus or bypass interlocks. Expected outcome: The mechanism receives a normal operating command under valid external conditions.

steps.title: 8. Observe Mechanical Operation During Bench Testing
steps.instructions: Using a controlled setup and appropriate test fluid, observe whether the accessible valve and roller-pump functions operate smoothly without unusual noise, binding, or repeated stopping. Keep hands and loose material away from moving parts. Expected outcome: Mechanical operation is smooth and repeatable.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify: Proper disposable loading Normal door closure Stable fluid delivery No abnormal noise No repeated mechanical fault indication Appropriate audible and visual alarms Expected outcome: The complete system operates normally. If all functions remain stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Mechanical Failure
steps.instructions: If a door, valve, or pumping mechanism remains jammed, intermittent, damaged, or nonfunctional after external causes are ruled out, remove the unit from service. Do not manually force, lubricate, realign, or disassemble internal drive components unless specifically authorized by service documentation and training. Expected outcome: The device is referred for qualified mechanical evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the RI-2 door would not close after installing the disposable.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found disposable tubing trapped in the door-loading area.
CCR.Resolution: The disposable was correctly repositioned, the door operated normally, and the unit passed fluid-delivery functional testing.

helpfulDetails: Affected door, valve, or pump function
Whether problem occurred without disposable installed

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Fluid-Out Alarm With Fluid Still Available
description: Troubleshoot source-container setup, tubing restrictions, disposable positioning, reservoir filling, and fluid-detection conditions when a fluid-out alarm occurs prematurely.

steps.title: 1. Maintain Patient Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not continue relying on an RI-2 that repeatedly indicates fluid out while fluid remains available. Move therapy to a verified alternative before troubleshooting if rapid infusion remains clinically required. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without dependence on an unreliable fluid-supply indication.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Record the exact alarm and determine whether fluid is visibly present in: The source container The disposable pathway The reservoir area The downstream tubing Determine whether the alarm occurred during priming or active delivery. Expected outcome: The point at which fluid appears to stop reaching the device is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Fluid Source
steps.instructions: Check the source container for: Adequate fluid Proper positioning A fully seated connection Collapsed or obstructed outlet Closed clamp Kinked tubing A container can contain fluid while still failing to supply it effectively. Expected outcome: Fluid can leave the source container without an external restriction.

steps.title: 4. Trace the Upstream Tubing
steps.instructions: Inspect the complete accessible path from the source toward the RI-2 for: Kinks Pinching Closed clamps Twisted tubing Compression by equipment or bedding Loose fittings Air locks or incomplete priming Expected outcome: The upstream pathway is open and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Check Disposable Loading
steps.instructions: Verify that the disposable is correctly installed and that tubing is fully seated at accessible guides, sensors, and loading locations. Incorrect seating may interfere with fluid movement or detection. Expected outcome: The disposable is correctly positioned without deformation or misrouting.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Reservoir Filling Behavior
steps.instructions: During a controlled bench setup, observe whether fluid enters and remains available in the disposable reservoir area as expected. If the reservoir does not fill despite an adequate source, recheck upstream flow and disposable condition. Expected outcome: Fluid progresses normally from the source into the disposable pathway.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Source and Disposable
steps.instructions: Use an appropriate test fluid source and known-good compatible disposable to separate device behavior from a faulty bag, connection, or disposable. Expected outcome: The fluid-out alarm does not occur while the known-good setup maintains fluid supply. If normal operation is restored, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Inspect Accessible Detection Areas
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible fluid-detection surfaces and tubing positions for contamination, moisture, residue, deformation, or improper seating. Do not insert objects into or adjust internal sensing components. Expected outcome: Accessible sensing areas are clean, unobstructed, and properly aligned with the disposable.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run the RI-2 under an appropriate bench test with adequate fluid available. Verify that: Fluid enters the system normally No premature fluid-out alarm occurs Flow remains stable Alarm indications remain functional Expected outcome: Fluid-out detection behaves consistently with actual fluid availability.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent False Fluid-Out Alarms
steps.instructions: If premature fluid-out alarms occur with multiple known-good disposables and a verified fluid source, remove the unit from service. Expected outcome: The device is held for qualified service rather than returned with unreliable fluid detection.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a fluid-out alarm even though the connected fluid bag was not empty.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the upstream tubing kinked between the fluid source and disposable.
CCR.Resolution: The restriction was corrected, the system was reprimed, and the RI-2 completed functional testing without a premature fluid-out alarm.

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Overtemperature Alarm or Delivered Fluid Too Warm
description: Troubleshoot overtemperature indications, disposable positioning, flow interruption, sensing conditions, and setup issues while preserving thermal patient safety.

steps.title: 1. Stop Use and Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Immediately stop relying on an RI-2 that indicates overtemperature or is suspected of delivering excessively warm fluid. Provide therapy through another verified device or method as clinically appropriate. Expected outcome: The patient is no longer exposed to potentially overheated fluid.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Alarm and Circumstances
steps.instructions: Document the displayed alarm or temperature indication and whether it occurred: During priming During active flow After flow interruption Immediately after startup Repeatedly with multiple setups Do not reset and return the device to use without determining whether the condition recurs. Expected outcome: The circumstances of the thermal event are clearly documented.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Disposable and Fluid Path
steps.instructions: Check for: Incorrect disposable loading Kinks Closed clamps Flow obstruction Empty fluid pathway sections Visible air Deformed tubing Restricted or interrupted flow can change heating conditions. Expected outcome: The fluid path is correctly loaded, fully primed, and unobstructed.

steps.title: 4. Verify Continuous Fluid Supply
steps.instructions: Confirm the source container contains fluid and that fluid can reach the RI-2 without restriction. Inspect upstream tubing and clamps. Expected outcome: Adequate fluid is available to the device continuously.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Temperature-Sensing Areas
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible disposable-seating and sensing surfaces for residue, contamination, moisture, or improper tubing contact. Do not open, adjust, or reposition internal temperature-sensing components. Expected outcome: No external condition is interfering with the sensing path.

steps.title: 6. Replace the Disposable
steps.instructions: Because the event involves temperature safety, replace a questionable disposable with a known-good compatible set before further functional testing. Expected outcome: A known-good disposable is installed correctly and fully primed.

steps.title: 7. Allow Normal Reset Conditions Before Retest
steps.instructions: Follow approved operating and service documentation for safe external reset or restart conditions. Do not repeatedly cycle power to suppress an overtemperature alarm without confirming the underlying condition. Expected outcome: The device is retested only after it is appropriate to do so.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Temperature Testing
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate bench setup and approved temperature-measurement equipment, evaluate the RI-2 independently of a patient. Observe temperature behavior and whether an overtemperature indication returns. Expected outcome: Temperature control remains stable and no inappropriate overtemperature condition recurs.

steps.title: 9. Verify Protective Alarm Function
steps.instructions: Confirm that temperature-related audible and visual indications operate correctly during approved functional testing. Never disable or bypass thermal protection to continue testing. Expected outcome: The protective system behaves normally and testing meets applicable service criteria.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Unexplained Overtemperature Condition
steps.instructions: If the device produced a credible overtemperature event or repeatedly alarms despite a correct known-good setup, remove it from service. Expected outcome: The unit is withheld from clinical use pending qualified thermal-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported an overtemperature alarm during RI-2 operation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the disposable tubing kinked, restricting flow through the external fluid path.
CCR.Resolution: The disposable was replaced and correctly routed, and the unit completed controlled temperature and functional testing without recurrence.

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Patient-Line Pressure High or Flow Rate Cannot Be Maintained
description: Troubleshoot downstream restrictions, tubing problems, connections, access limitations, disposable issues, and setup conditions causing high pressure or inadequate flow.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not continue forcing rapid infusion against unexplained high downstream pressure. If the patient requires ongoing rapid fluid delivery, transition to another verified delivery path or device according to clinical direction. Expected outcome: Patient therapy does not depend on a pressurized or unreliable infusion pathway.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Record whether the issue is: A displayed high-pressure condition Flow that decreases below the intended setting Intermittent flow limitation A problem occurring only with a particular patient line or accessory Note the exact displayed information without inventing a cause. Expected outcome: The pressure or flow complaint is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Patient-Line Tubing
steps.instructions: Trace the complete accessible downstream tubing path. Look for: Kinks Closed clamps Pinched tubing Tight bends Compression under equipment Twisted connectors Obstructed accessories Expected outcome: The downstream pathway is physically open and unrestricted. If a restriction is corrected and normal flow returns during verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check External Connections and Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect all patient-line connectors, extensions, filters, adapters, and other external components being used. A narrow, obstructed, damaged, or incorrectly connected accessory can increase resistance. Expected outcome: All accessories are appropriate, securely connected, and free of visible obstruction or damage.

steps.title: 5. Separate Device Function From Patient Access
steps.instructions: Do not diagnose or manipulate patient vascular access as a Clinical Engineering repair task. If pressure rises only when connected to the patient but the RI-2 performs normally on a controlled test setup, return the clinical access question to the appropriate care team. Expected outcome: A device-related flow problem is distinguished from resistance downstream of the equipment.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the Disposable
steps.instructions: Check the disposable for: Kinking Collapsed tubing Incorrect routing Visible deformation Damage Improper loading Replace a questionable disposable with a known-good compatible set. Expected outcome: The disposable presents no visible restriction and is correctly loaded.

steps.title: 7. Verify Source-Side Fluid Delivery
steps.instructions: Check the fluid source and upstream path for adequate supply, open clamps, and unrestricted flow. Insufficient upstream filling can also result in poor delivered flow even when downstream pressure is normal. Expected outcome: Fluid reaches the RI-2 freely from the source.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Controlled Bench Load
steps.instructions: Using appropriate test equipment and an approved test setup, evaluate fluid delivery independently of the patient circuit. Do not rely on clinical observation alone to determine whether the device can maintain flow. Expected outcome: The RI-2 delivers fluid consistently under the controlled setup without unexplained high-pressure behavior.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify that the device: Maintains stable operation Responds appropriately to external flow conditions Produces normal audible and visual indications Does not exhibit unexplained pressure or flow limitation Expected outcome: Normal flow performance is demonstrated. If the issue is resolved and repeatable functional testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unexplained Pressure or Flow Failure
steps.instructions: If abnormal pressure indications or poor flow continue with an unobstructed test setup, known-good disposable, and appropriate test equipment, remove the device from service. Expected outcome: A potentially unsafe flow-control problem is escalated for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported high patient-line pressure and reduced flow during rapid infusion.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the downstream tubing sharply kinked near an external connector.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing restriction was eliminated, and the RI-2 maintained normal flow during bench functional verification.

helpfulDetails: Whether issue occurred only on patient connection

title: Belmont Medical Technologies Rapid Infuser RI-2 Rapid Infuser - Reservoir, Heat Exchanger, or Patient-Line Leak
description: Locate external fluid leaks, loose connections, disposable damage, poor seating, and cracked accessories while determining whether the RI-2 itself requires service.

steps.title: 1. Stop Use and Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Stop using the RI-2 if blood, fluid, or other liquid is leaking from the disposable pathway or device. Maintain therapy using another verified method if needed. Use appropriate precautions for blood or body-fluid exposure. Expected outcome: The patient and staff are protected from continued leakage and unreliable fluid delivery.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Leak Location
steps.instructions: Without opening the device, determine whether fluid appears to originate from: Source connection Reservoir area Heat-exchange disposable Patient-line tubing External connector Disposable-to-device interface Inside the equipment enclosure If fluid appears to have entered the device enclosure, disconnect the unit from use and stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The leak is localized to an external disposable component or identified as possible internal fluid intrusion.

steps.title: 3. Inspect All External Connections
steps.instructions: Check fluid-source, reservoir, disposable, and patient-line connections for: Loose fittings Cross-threading Incomplete engagement Damaged connectors Improper accessory attachment Expected outcome: All external connections are properly seated and dry.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Disposable
steps.instructions: Remove the disposable from service and inspect for: Cuts Punctures Cracked components Split tubing Leaking seams Deformation Damage from incorrect loading Do not attempt to repair a disposable. Expected outcome: Any damaged disposable is identified and replaced.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Loading Area for External Damage
steps.instructions: Check accessible surfaces for sharp edges, broken guides, damaged doors, or other visible conditions that could pinch or damage the disposable. Expected outcome: No external device damage is present that could cause disposable leakage.

steps.title: 6. Install a Known-Good Disposable
steps.instructions: After the device is cleaned and dried appropriately, install a new compatible disposable using an approved bench test fluid. Prime the system while watching closely for leakage. Expected outcome: The known-good disposable remains dry throughout priming. If leakage does not recur and the unit passes verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Check for Pressure-Related External Restrictions
steps.instructions: Inspect downstream tubing, clamps, and accessories for restrictions that could contribute to excessive pressure and leakage at a weak connection. Expected outcome: The fluid path is unobstructed and connections remain secure during flow.

steps.title: 8. Evaluate for Fluid Intrusion
steps.instructions: If fluid was found beneath covers, in vents, around electrical interfaces, or in areas not intended to become wet, remove the device from service. Do not energize or continue operating equipment with suspected internal fluid intrusion. Expected outcome: A potentially contaminated or electrically unsafe device is isolated for bench evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Leak and Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With an appropriate nonpatient test setup, verify that: The disposable remains dry Connections remain secure Fluid delivery remains stable No leak develops during representative operation Normal alarm and control functions remain available Expected outcome: No external leak is present and device operation remains normal.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent or Device-Origin Leakage
steps.instructions: If leakage recurs with a known-good disposable or appears to originate from the device rather than the disposable, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from clinical service for qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported fluid leaking from the RI-2 disposable reservoir area during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged disposable component leaking during priming.
CCR.Resolution: The disposable was replaced, the system was reprimed, and leak and functional testing were completed successfully.

helpfulDetails: Whether leak occurred during prime or delivery
